questions.q: Who makes you laugh the most?
questions.answer: My grandfather, surprisingly. He's in his eighties but still incredibly sharp, and he has a wonderfully [[dry sense of humour]]. He'll say something outrageous with a completely straight face, and the whole family ends up in fits of laughter.

questions.q: Do you like watching comedy shows?
questions.answer: Yes, I love a good laugh at the end of a long day. Comedy is the easiest way for me to switch off. I especially enjoy clever, [[observational]] humour that plays on everyday situations.

questions.q: Are you good at telling jokes?
questions.answer: Not especially. I always rush the punchline or start laughing before I finish. I'm much better at [[witty]] remarks in the moment, reacting to what's happening around me, than at telling a prepared joke.

questions.q: What did you find funny when you were a child?
questions.answer: Mostly slapstick, like cartoons where characters fell over or got chased. My sister and I used to watch Mr Bean together and laugh until our stomachs hurt. That kind of physical comedy is [[universally]] funny, I think.

questions.q: Do you think humour is different in different cultures?
questions.answer: Definitely. A lot of humour depends on wordplay and shared references, so it often gets [[lost in translation]]. I've noticed that some Bengali jokes simply don't work in English, however carefully I try to explain them.
